topStories.headline: Central SoMa's 725 Harrison Site Asks Planning Commission for 18 More Months — and Takes a Promised Affordable Housing Parcel With It
topStories.dek: The sponsor of a key Central SoMa office tower appeared before the Planning Commission on September 24 seeking an extension that would push its nearly one-million-square-foot approval to March 2028, while a land parcel meant to produce 144 affordable homes waits alongside it.
topStories.body:
One of the linchpin development sites of the 2018 Central SoMa Plan returned to the San Francisco Planning Commission on Thursday, September 24 — not to break ground, but to ask for more time. The sponsor of the approved project at 725–765 Harrison Street requested an 18-month extension of its Large Project Authorization to March 24, 2028, under items 7a, 7b and 7c on the commission's agenda. Planning staff recommended approval with conditions.

The approved project is 14 stories, 185 feet tall, and contains roughly 981,000 gross square feet — approximately 810,000 of it designated office space. The entitlement was originally approved on December 12, 2019, and modified in June 2022. The reason for the delay is no mystery: San Francisco's citywide office vacancy rate stood at 29.2 percent in the second quarter of 2026, according to CBRE — compared with roughly 3 percent when the Central SoMa Plan was adopted.

What rides with the extension is a land dedication of roughly 15,000 square feet promised to the Mayor's Office of Housing. That parcel was intended to generate 144 affordable homes. It has been waiting since 2019, and if the commission approved the extension as staff recommended, it waits another 18 months. The Central SoMa Plan was originally projected to deliver close to 16 million square feet of housing and jobs, 33 percent affordable, across the blocks between the Financial District and Oracle Park.

The vote occurred at noon in Room 416 of City Hall. My Town News will report the commission's decision as the record becomes available.

topStories.headline: Treasure Island's Proposed Unit-Count Expansion Heads Toward Board of Supervisors — Developer Wants Sign-Off Before End of 2026
topStories.dek: A revised plan to add as many as 2,800 homes to Treasure Island's approved build-out — pushing the total to 10,800 units — is moving through city channels as the development's first phase, centered on the newly opened 490 Avenue of the Palms, shows the neighborhood beginning to take shape.
topStories.body:
Treasure Island Community Development is pushing for Board of Supervisors approval before the end of 2026 on a revised plan that would increase the island's total housing count by as much as 35 percent, from 8,000 homes to as many as 10,800, according to a February 2026 TIDA board document. The revised proposal, discussed in a January 30 San Francisco Chronicle report, aims to capitalize on momentum the island has built over the past several years.

That momentum is visible. Phase one of the redevelopment officially wrapped in July 2026 with the opening of 490 Avenue of the Palms, a six-story building offering 148 residences along the island's waterfront. The building — the first new residential for-sale offering on Treasure Island — was co-developed by a partnership of Lennar Corporation, Stockbridge Capital Group, and Wilson Meany. Its two neighboring completed communities, Isle House and Hawkins, are now each more than 90 percent leased, and nearly a thousand residents have moved into newly built homes across Treasure and Yerba Buena islands in recent years.

The islands now have eight completed parks, a functioning ferry terminal offering a roughly 10-minute commute to the Ferry Building, and Muni Line 25 connecting residents to the Transit Center. The full build-out plan envisions up to 8,000 — and now potentially 10,800 — homes alongside 300 acres of parks and open space. The Treasure Island Development Authority's TIDA board document notes that the increased units would be rental, with many added in the next phase of construction, some of which could start as soon as this year.

topStories.headline: Giants Close Out the Season at Oracle Park with Fan Appreciation Weekend and a Final Farewell to Broadcaster Mike Krukow
topStories.dek: The San Francisco Giants host the Los Angeles Dodgers this weekend in the team's last three home games of 2026, with the Willie Mac Award ceremony tonight, a Fiesta Gigantes celebration Saturday, and broadcaster Mike Krukow's final game Sunday.
topStories.body:
Oracle Park hosts the San Francisco Giants' final homestand of the 2026 regular season this weekend, a three-game series against the Los Angeles Dodgers running from Friday through Sunday. The team was eliminated from playoff contention on September 6 following a loss to the New York Mets — the fifth consecutive season without a postseason appearance — but the weekend carries its own significance for the ballpark's Mission Bay neighbors and the wider fan base.

Tonight, Friday September 25, features the 2026 Willie Mac Award Ceremony in a pregame presentation on the field. The award, named for Giants legend Willie McCovey, honors the most inspirational player on the team as voted by players, coaches, training staff, and fans. First pitch is at 7:15 PM.

Saturday, September 26 (1:05 PM) is the final Fiesta Gigantes of the season, with Latin music, culture, and food throughout the ballpark. The first 10,000 fans through the gates will receive a fan-favorite giveaway from the 2026 season. Sunday, September 27 (12:05 PM) is the final game of the year — and, more notably, the final broadcast for color analyst Mike Krukow, who is retiring after 36 years in the Giants' broadcast booth as one half of the beloved Kruk and Kuip duo.

events.title: SFMOMA: RM Exhibition — Works from the BTS Member's Personal Collection
events.description: SFMOMA hosts the first museum exhibition drawn from K-pop global superstar RM's personal collection, filling the museum's seventh floor with nearly 200 works by modern and contemporary Korean artists alongside international pieces — several never before shown publicly in the U.S. Opens October 3.

moreNews.headline: Treasure Island Gets New Executive Director as Unit-Expansion Proposal Advances
moreNews.body: City Administrator Carmen Chu appointed Sheela Jivan as Executive Director of the Treasure Island Development Authority on May 7, 2026, following the January retirement of longtime director Robert Beck, who served more than 30 years in the role. Jivan takes over as TIDA pursues Board of Supervisors sign-off — sought before the end of 2026 — on a revised development agreement that would increase the island's planned housing from 8,000 to as many as 10,800 units.

moreNews.headline: SFMTA Moving Ahead with Metered Parking Implementation on Treasure and Yerba Buena Islands
moreNews.body: Following a March 3, 2026 vote by the SFMTA Board of Directors approving on-street metered parking for Treasure Island and Yerba Buena Island, the agency is now partnering with TIDA to prepare an implementation plan. SFMTA will post a detailed timeline as it becomes available. The metered parking program is designed to manage growing vehicle traffic as the islands' population increases with new residential development.
